title: Two arms of immunity
objective: Contrast innate and adaptive immunity by speed, specificity and memory.

steps.title: Fast and general vs slow and specific
steps.body:
The immune system has two cooperating arms:

- **[[innate immunity|Innate]]:** fast (minutes to hours), uses prebuilt general-purpose sensors, no lasting memory. First responders.
- **[[adaptive immunity|Adaptive]]:** slow the first time (days), exquisitely specific, and remembers. T and B cells (B2).

Innate buys time and then instructs the adaptive response.

steps.prompt: Match each feature to the right arm.
steps.explanation: Speed and generality vs specificity and memory is the core contrast; everything else in immunology hangs off it.

steps.title: Why neuroscientists care
steps.body:
Nervous and immune systems talk constantly. Sensory neurons can detect the same danger signals innate immune cells detect, and immune cells respond to neurotransmitters and neuropeptides.

Track B builds the immunology you need to read that crosstalk, which is central to the gut and to inflammation-driven changes in sensation (A9).

steps.prompt: A splinter gets infected within an hour, with redness and swelling before any antibody appears. Which arm is acting?
steps.explanation: Fast, non-specific inflammation with no antibodies yet is the innate response. Antibodies (adaptive) take days on first exposure.

variants.setup: A cut turns red, warm and swollen within an hour — long before any antibody could be made.
variants.prompt: Which arm of immunity is responding?
variants.reveal: Fast, non-specific inflammation with no antibodies yet is the innate response; adaptive antibodies take days on a first exposure.

steps.setup: A mouse is engineered to lack all T and B cells but keeps innate immunity.
steps.prompt: What do you expect on first exposure to a common microbe?
options: No response at all, since every arm of immunity has been removed
An early innate response, but no specific or long-term immunity
Perfect immunity, as the innate system fully compensates for the loss
Only antibody production, with no inflammation or phagocyte activity
steps.reveal: Innate defenses still work, so there's an early response, but without adaptive cells the animal can't mount specific, memory-based immunity. This is roughly the situation in some immunodeficient mouse strains.

variants.prompt: A mouse lacking all T and B cells meets a common microbe for the first time. What happens?
options: No response at all, since every arm of immunity has been removed
An early innate response, but no specific or long-term immunity
Perfect immunity, as the innate system fully compensates for the loss
Only antibody production, with no inflammation or phagocyte activity
variants.explanation: Innate defenses still fire, giving an early response; without adaptive cells there is no specific, memory-based immunity.
